title: Flight 19
hook: In 1945, five Navy bombers vanished during a routine training flight.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: Five torpedo bombers took off from Florida on a clear afternoon.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: The lead pilot radioed that his compass was not working.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Static and confusion filled the radio as the planes flew further off course.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: A rescue plane sent to find them vanished too, with thirteen men aboard.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: The official report blamed navigator error and worsening weather that night.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: To this day, no wreckage from any of the six aircraft has ever been found.

end.line: So what really happened to Flight 19?

description: In December 1945, five Navy bombers vanished over the Atlantic during a training flight, and the plane sent to find them disappeared too.

facts.claim: Flight 19 was a training flight of five TBM Avenger torpedo bombers that disappeared on 5 December 1945 after leaving Naval Air Station Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
The flight leader reported his compass was malfunctioning and the group became lost over the Atlantic.
Radio transmissions grew increasingly confused as the crews debated their position before contact was lost.
A PBM Mariner flying boat sent to search for the missing planes also vanished, with thirteen men aboard.
A Navy board of investigation blamed navigator error and deteriorating weather for the loss.
No confirmed wreckage from any of the six aircraft has ever been recovered.
